title: Eating Plan Linked to Slower Brain Aging, Study Finds
summary:
As people get older, their brains slowly change. Some parts shrink, and fluid-filled spaces called ventricles get bigger. Scientists wanted to know whether food might play a role.

A new study looked at the MIND diet. It mixes parts of the Mediterranean diet with an eating plan designed to lower blood pressure. The plan stresses green leafy vegetables, other vegetables, berries, nuts, whole grains, fish, beans, olive oil and poultry. It recommends limiting butter, cheese, red meat, sweets and fried fast foods.

The researchers followed people for an average of 12 years. The people had regular health checks, answered questions about what they ate, and had MRI brain scans. An MRI is a machine that takes pictures of the inside of the body.

Everyone showed the normal changes that come with age. But people whose eating matched the MIND diet more closely lost grey matter more slowly. Grey matter is brain tissue that helps with memory, learning and decision making. Each 3 point rise in diet score was linked to 20% less age-related decline, which the researchers said is like 2.5 years of delayed brain aging. Eating more berries was linked to slower growth of the ventricles. Eating more sweets and fried fast foods was linked to more shrinking in the hippocampus, a brain area involved in memory.

These results show a link, not proof that food causes the changes. The study was published in the Journal of Neurology Neurosurgery & Psychiatry.
why_it_matters: The study adds to the idea that what people eat over many years may be connected to how their brains age, even though more research is needed to show cause and effect.
